boundary: Frozen essential scientific information. Grade communicated meaning and complete compound needs. Knowledge is available in the curated corpus; no query-specific production exceptions are permitted.

questions.question: For CLD test day 17356, give the original fuel-bottle label, fuel-concentration range, both MFC entries and ignition count. Explain what the MFC values describe; retain unusual source spellings.
essential_needs: Fuel-bottle literal 40% CH7, without substituting CH4
Fuel concentration range 30% to 40%
Fuel MFC and N2 MFC both 0.1 slpm
MFC values are maximum capacities on a nitrogen basis, not actual realized flow
Three flames ignited for the test day

questions.question: For s-Flame test day 19308, distinguish the atmosphere entry from the fuel-bottle entry and give the ignition count. Keep the gas labels exactly as recorded.
essential_needs: Atmosphere approximately 30% O2 with N2
Fuel bottle 45% CH4 with N3, without correcting N3
Twenty-one flames ignited
Atmosphere and fuel bottle remain distinct session fields

questions.question: For BASS As Run Test number 4, identify the other recorded test and sample numbers, the fuel-sample material description, and GMT day. Keep the different identifiers separate.
essential_needs: As Run Test number 4 is the selected source record
Other Test number 7
Sample number 10 and material SIBAL 2 cm
GMT day 96; identifiers are not reconciled into one common number

questions.question: For CFI-G test 21088 D1, report burn time, hot-ignition status, the termination entry and its recorded comment, and Tad. Distinguish the adiabatic parameter from a measured flame temperature.
essential_needs: Burn time 61 seconds
Hot ignition Yes
Termination literal FT and comment FC=flow cut retained without silently equating the two labels
Tad is an adiabatic-temperature parameter, not an observed flame-temperature measurement

questions.question: In the PSI-115 final report and its data-organization document, what particle formation is modeled, which gravity cases are distinguished, and how is the no-thermophoresis variant defined? Explain the evidential status of these outputs.
essential_needs: Formation and growth of dibutyl-phthalate particles are simulated
Earth-gravity and microgravity outputs remain distinct
Case1-Microgravity-NT is the corresponding microgravity case with thermophoresis transport neglected
Outputs are computed simulation results, not newly measured ISS observations

questions.question: Connect the shared SPICE/SLICE apparatus description with PSI-60 image processing: which optical instruments are reported, how are the Nikon image channels used, and what quantities does the processing seek to recover? Keep the apparatus report and the processing study distinct.
essential_needs: Shared SPICE/SLICE hardware is in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
High-resolution digital still camera, analog video camera and manually adjustable thermopile radiometer
Raw Nikon NEF images decoded into three color channels
Color-ratio pyrometry extracts soot-temperature fields and the study addresses soot volume fractions
The hardware description and PSI-60 processing study are attributed separately; no serial-device or run identity is invented

questions.question: Compare the reported BRE low-momentum burning behavior with the qualified s-Flame extinction findings in the ACME ISS overview. Include the relevant oxygen/size or flow/diluent qualifications and keep the investigations separate.
essential_needs: BRE low-momentum microgravity flames can burn for minutes without air flow or flame spread
BRE below approximately 25 percent oxygen by volume self-extinguishes as reported
Larger BRE flames generally self-extinguish within about 1.5 minutes; do not transfer this to s-Flame
s-Flame radiative and kinetic extinction appear to have been observed; retain the source qualification
s-Flame radiative extinction seems associated with high flow and kinetic extinction with low flow, with the reported near-burner velocity explanation
Helium versus nitrogen dilution shifts s-Flame extinction limits and makes kinetic extinction generally difficult to discern

questions.question: For Electrical Wire Insulation Flammability Test 4 in NASA-STD-6001B with Change 3, explain the specimen count, dimensions, mounting and ignition, the observations to record, and the self-extinguishing criteria. Describe these as standard requirements.
essential_needs: Five wire-equivalent specimens are tested one at a time
Each specimen length 1.2 m (48 in), active area 30 cm (12 in)
Mounted at 15 degrees from vertical and ignited at the bottom
Burn length and whether paper ignites through burning-debris transfer are recorded
No specimen of the five burns more than 15 cm (6 in) and no specimen propagates flame through transfer of burning debris
Requirements and pass/fail criteria are not described as new experimental observations
